text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] auth anomaly: edge-proxy reports spike of 401s (≈3.2k in 5m). Samples show repeated token reuse from same svcacct id. Logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/query?q=auth+401+edge-proxy. Runbook: /runbooks/auth-spike

maya-oncall: ack — I'm looking now, pulling top hosts and tenants. Will post samples.

maya-oncall: quick sample (running locally):
```
$ grep \"401\" /var/log/proxy/edge-2026-03-18.log | head -n 10
2026-03-18T17:02:12Z edge-1 svc-rotation-234 token=*** path=/v1/infer status=401
2026-03-18T17:02:12Z edge-2 svc-rotation-234 token=*** path=/v1/chat status=401
...
```

raj-sec: seeing repeated token id svc-rotation-234 across IPs. Patterns look like token replay (same token used after TTL expiry). Could be stale cache honoring old tokens at legacy-auth.

taylor-platform: if legacy-auth cache is serving old payloads we should flush region caches. I'm about to run the flush playbook for us-east-1. Also prepping rotation for svc-rotation-234. @maya-oncall any customers flagged?

cs-lead: provisional: two enterprise tenants reported intermittent 403->500s in the last 10m but no data exfil reports. I'll open a watch ticket and ping their CSMs.

legal: preserve all logs and tag them for potential preservation. DO NOT purge anything until we confirm. Need list of affected tenant ids when available.

maya-oncall: @taylor-platform runbook command used:
```
kubectl -n infra exec deploy/auth-cache -- /bin/flush-cache --region=us-east-1
```

taylor-platform: flush initiated -> response: \"flush OK (us-east-1)\". Now rotating svc token: creating new credential and updating secret-manager. Rotation steps: create new token, update service secret, restart short-lived pods, monitor.

taylor-platform: rotation done for svc-rotation-234 -> new token issued at 2026-03-18T17:08:05Z. Updated secret: secret://prod/svc-rotation-234. Restarted 3 replicas.

maya-oncall: metrics: 401 rate dropped to baseline within ~90s after flush/rotate. No spike in egress traffic seen to external buckets.

raj-sec: good containment. Next steps: 1) rotate any service tokens older than 30d (I will open infra-rotation ticket), 2) revoke long-lived sessions, 3) run quick audit for suspicious API callers in last 24h.

cs-lead: I'll keep customers informed under a watch update; will only send broader comms if customers confirm impact.

legal: thanks. once raj posts the tenant list, I'll confirm whether we need formal notifications.

incident-bot: Severity set to sev3 (auth noise contained, no confirmed leakage). Pager cleared. Filing followups: infra-rotate-714159 (ticket link: https://tickets.internal/infra/714159).

maya-oncall: closing timeline note: root cause likely stale token acceptance due to legacy cache not respecting TTL. Action items assigned in ticket. :thumbsup:
